notes: Legacy 'pre-defined-allergies'-coded SNOMED concepts (315 total, minus 416098002 'Medicine allergy' which belongs on rules/allergy-junk-codes.json instead, not here -- 314 entries) and their reviewed conversion target, used by content-scripts/allergy-cleanup.js's 'Clean up allergies?' widget to suggest a substance conversion for any active allergy with allergyCodeType 'pre-defined-allergies'. Hand-built from two spreadsheets Nick reviewed personally (true-allergy-conversion-candidates.csv, 128 rows under SNOMED's genuine allergy root; adverse-reaction-decomposition.csv, 187 rows under the separate adverse-reaction root -- confirmed distinct hierarchies, no conceptId overlap) -- see the project memory for the full sweep/review history. `kind` is one of: 'substance' (straight conversion, no reaction override), 'substance-plus-reaction' (decompose to substance + a reaction search seed -- `reaction.text` is a plain search hint, never a pre-resolved conceptId, the reaction picker always searches live), 'not-convertible' (no dm+d code exists for this class, or nothing nameable from the code text at all -- `notes` explains why, offered for manual search only, no pre-filled suggestion), 'not-an-allergy' (miscoded -- not offered for conversion at all, `notes` explains the real condition and recommends removal via the junk-removal flow instead). VTM-preference policy (prefer the plain generic/VTM-level substance over a specific salt/dose-form/branded one) already applied when these were resolved -- do not re-derive picks here, this file is the reviewed output, not raw search results. Matched by EXACT conceptId only, same discipline as every other list in this codebase.

entries.notes: Originally mapped to the bare 'Chloroquine' substance concept (373468005), but that isn't a real product-level/VTM concept -- dm+d only models Chloroquine at the salt level (sulfate/phosphate), with no unsalted product. Corrected to 'Chloroquine only product' (775187003), the broadest product-level concept that doesn't commit to one specific salt. If the specific salt is known (sulfate vs phosphate), that's a genuine clinical distinction worth recording instead.

Salt-ambiguous (2026-08-02 pre-merge review): dm+d splits perindopril into two salt VTMs (erbumine and arginine) with no salt-neutral parent, and an ACE-inhibitor pseudoallergy (cough/angioedema) is a CLASS effect -- pre-selecting erbumine (22209011000001101, the previous mapping) would not alert on a perindopril-arginine prescription. Search live for 'perindopril' and pick the salt the patient actually received (or record both salts if unknown -- the class signal matters more than the salt).
